_source: Rise Fall Repeat Short, watched in the built-in browser 2026-11-19: frames at 0/0.5/1/2/3/5 s, a frame at the middle of every shot (33 shots from the probe's cut list), a 0.5 s burst at the figure card (99.5-100.5 s), word timings from YouTube's caption track, audio probe over the full 140 s. Our own descriptions. 2.2M views. YouTube marks it 'AI' (altered or synthetic content): every picture is a generated cinematic still.

lines.gist: the studio risked it all on an unwanted hero and built a huge empire
mid-90s the comics company was near bankruptcy after years of bad deals
its best heroes had been licensed away; rivals got rich while it watched
so it chose to fund its own films, with no studio partner
it borrowed from a bank against its remaining characters; failure meant losing all
Hollywood mocked them and even their own board worried
they picked a minor character test audiences didn't know and hired a director
they also cast an actor Hollywood had written off
filming started half-written and early screenings went badly, but audiences loved the lead
the first film made several times its budget worldwide
a post-credit tease launched a shared universe and the team-up films made billions
a giant entertainment company bought them; the franchise earned tens of billions
lesson: back yourself when others don't; follow for more business stories

ending.cta: follow for more real business stories
ending.lastFrame: a man from behind on a mountain top at sunset with a 3-word caption

whyItWorks: The title is the hook line and both name the company and the bet in the first two seconds.
A new still every 4.2 s with a constant slow push; cuts land on sound hits (20 of 33).
Captions are 1-3 bold white capitals with the key word yellow, centred low-middle, one beat at a time.
The big figure gets its own gold poster card; every other figure only lives in the caption.
